items_missed: No pricing delivered at all on the call - the entire Pricing/Differentiators section was skipped and pushed to an offline email ('I'll provide the two estimates ... off-line and then I'll send you the quote via email')
No hourly rate, no what's-included list (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap pads, bands, tools), no disassembly/reassembly, no packing service pricing
No No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000) explanation
No clock explanation - clock start, 2.5 hour minimum, 15-minute prorated increments, sense-check all absent
No estimate framing - no typical time range for the home size, no number of movers or trucks
No trip fee / drive time discussion despite a New Braunfels-to-Austin (Barton Creek) haul that is roughly 60 miles
No assembly/disassembly discussion despite three IKEA entertainment cabinets being the heaviest items
Save Your Ass prep speech entirely absent - especially costly here, since the customer is self-packing most of the nick-nacks and is already downsizing

Never asked about stairs/floors at the origin house, additional rooms (garage, storage unit, balcony), long walks or narrow hallways, elevator/parking/HOA access at the destination apartment, or storage stops
Never asked the moving-stressor question ('anything you're particularly worried about?')
No booking attempt - mentioned the September 6 opening in the opener but never came back to close it
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?' and never gave hours or how to reach the team
Never used the customer's name (Aaron) once - used 'sir' a single time
top_strength: The inventory intake was genuinely well-run - Amy walked the customer room by room ('let's start at the living area and then the room'), gave him room to think ('Take your time, no rush'), and used a smart benchmark to land the box count (50-60 boxes for a full 1600 sqft home vs. 15-25 for a one-bedroom) so a hesitant customer could answer with confidence.
coaching_note: Amy did the discovery and then hung up before selling anything - no rate, no differentiators, no clock, no estimate. She had every detail she needed to quote on the phone; the fix is to build the estimate live on the call and walk him through it, because a quote that arrives cold in an inbox loses the No Worries / Meet Your Mover / On-Time Guarantee story entirely.
phone_presence_notes: Pleasant and patient with a few real warmth markers ('thank you so much for asking', 'Take your time, no rush'), but heavily filled with 'Mm-hmm' backchannel, no name use, and no rapport moment beyond the task.
